title: Implement resumable offset checkpoints and opportunistic prefetch for cross-tenant bridges
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our current ingest bridges that fan messages from Kafka into Redis-backed consumer queues lack robust resume semantics and suffer duplicate redelivery during consumer restarts and transient failures. The consumer path mixes retry scheduling and inflight bookkeeping, which creates head-of-line sensitivity and complicates backpressure behavior. This ticket proposes two coordinated refactors: 1) Introduce resumable offset checkpoints (per-tenant resume points stored atomically) so workers can resume from an exact durable position with fast catch-up, and 2) Add an opportunistic prefetch layer that pulls safe-ahead messages into a local prefetch buffer without increasing commit surface area. Goals: reduce duplicate deliveries, shorten cold-start warmup for workers, and decouple delayed-retry allocation from the hot consumer path.
acceptance_criteria: Resumable checkpoints written atomically per-tenant to Redis with versioned keys and Lua-based CAS to avoid races
Worker startup resumes from stored checkpoint and only processes messages with offsets > checkpoint
Duplicate redelivery rate (measured at consumer confirmation) reduced by >= 90% in restart scenarios
Prefetch buffer reduces first-request P95 latency during burst recoveries by >= 30% without increasing memory usage beyond configured limits
Delayed-retry allocator runs on a separate scheduler/executor and does not add to consumer event-loop latency (measured by event-loop stalls metric)
rollout_plan: Prototype: implement checkpoint write/read and local prefetch buffer behind feature flags (dev env) - 1 week
Integration: enable checkpointing for a small set of non-critical tenants (canary) and monitor duplicates/latency - 1 week
Hardening: tune prefetch window, eviction policy, and TTLs; add migration job to backfill checkpoints for active partitions - 4 days
Full rollout: enable for all dedicated and hosted bridges with telemetry gates and automatic rollback on failure - 3 days
risks: Race conditions if checkpoint updates are not atomic - mitigated by Lua CAS and version tags
Increased Redis write volume under high churn - mitigated by batching checkpoint writes and configurable checkpoint frequency
Prefetch may increase memory usage or pull unneeded messages for low-throughput tenants - mitigated by tenant-specific prefetch caps and adaptive backpressure
Migration complexity for partitions with legacy lease semantics - mitigation: phased backfill and fallback to legacy behavior per partition
related_links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/bridges/resume-design - design doc with state machine and Lua scripts
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem on 2026-02-16 restart storm. Initial design captured in Confluence link.
2026-02-22 Marco Li: Spike complete. Lua CAS approach looks viable; prototype can write checkpoints at partition level. Observed 5-7ms p95 on Redis writes - acceptable.
2026-02-25 QA: Requesting test harness for restart scenarios that simulates consumer eviction and lease migration. Adding integration tests to pipeline.
2026-03-03 Marco Li: Implemented local prefetch buffer behind flag. Observed 35% reduction in cold-start P95 for canary tenant A. Memory cap enforced and tested under burst.
2026-03-07 Security: Reviewed Redis key naming; suggested tenant-scoped prefixes and KMS access pattern review. No blocker.
2026-03-10 Infra: Noted potential Redis capacity spike if checkpoint frequency is aggressive. Agreed to batch checkpoint writes every 2s per partition and provide opt-out.

2026-03-12 Marco Li: Rolling canary to 10% of tenants. Monitoring duplicates and event-loop stalls. Next: backfill script for active partitions and add circuit-breaker to disable prefetch when memory pressure high.
